newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares start out firm, shrug off dollar.
newsitem.headline: German shares start out firm, shrug off dollar.

text.p: German shares got the week off to a surprisingly firm start on Monday, shrugging off further declines in the dollar in early trade as selected blue chip stocks led by Deutsche Telekom AG posted firm gains.
The IBIS DAX index was up 18.63 points, or 0.5 percent, at 3,551.84 points an hour and a half into pre-bourse dealings.

Deutsche Telekom, benefitting from interest ahead of its annual news conference on Tuesday and other factors, extended Friday's gains to set a new all-time high of 41.95 marks in early trade. The shares were up nearly five percent at 41.75 marks at 0750 GMT.
With 1.5 million shares traded in the early session, Telekom's turnover led the field.
Dealers noted that Telekom was approaching a six-month deadline on May 19, after which its shares could be sold without incurring tax.
In addition, a report in Der Spiegel magazine at the weekend that the company was moving into commercial television in a bid to turn to profit on its cable business was well received.
"The share's move above 40 marks was an important psychological factor as well," said another dealer.
Airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG also continued its recent advance after announcing its first ever first quarter profit last week. It shares were up 36 pfennigs, or 1.3 percent, at 28.45 marks.
Some dealers were sceptical whether the market could hold its early gains through the day.
"With such a limited focus, it's hard to be confident. I could see the dollar impact gaining a bit more force as the day goes on," said one.
At 1.6841 marks, the dollar was notably feeble, but most share dealers said it was still in an acceptable range.
Among smaller shares, preferred shares in process technology supplier GEA AG rose two percent to 612 marks in early trade.
The company had said it expected a clear increase in earnings this year and said it would pay an unchanged dividend on 1996 earnings.
